actions.name: gain initial access through exploitation of web servers
actions.description: The actors gain initial access through widespread exploitation of web servers through known vulnerabilities, such as CVE-2021-44228 (“Log4Shell”) in Apache’s Log4j software library and other CVEs listed, to deploy web shells and gain access to sensitive information and applications for further exploitation.

actions.name: deploy web shell malware
actions.description: The actors deploy web shell malware on victim web servers to execute arbitrary system commands.

actions.name: perform system discovery and enumeration
actions.description: The actors perform system, network, and account enumeration using native tools such as Windows command line, PowerShell, WMIC, and Linux bash, including netstat commands.

actions.name: establish persistence using Scheduled Tasks
actions.description: The actors establish persistence on compromised systems using Scheduled Tasks.

actions.name: perform privilege escalation using credential stealing tools
actions.description: The actors perform privilege escalation using common credential stealing tools such as Mimikatz, Dumpert, and ProcDump, and by accessing the Active Directory domain database through targeting of the NTDS.dit file.

actions.name: use custom malware implants and remote access tools
actions.description: The actors deploy and leverage custom malware implants and remote access tools (RATs) for execution, lateral movement, and data exfiltration.

actions.name: conduct phishing activity using malicious attachments
actions.description: The actors conduct phishing activity using malicious attachments, including Microsoft Windows Shortcut File (LNK) files or HTML Application (HTA) script files inside encrypted or unencrypted zip archives.

actions.name: use system logging for discovery and lateral movement
actions.description: The actors log active window changes, clipboard data, and keystrokes and save the collected logging information to the %Temp% directory to aid in discovery and lateral movement.

actions.name: use Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) for lateral movement
actions.description: The actors have used Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) to move laterally within victim networks.

actions.name: use Server Message Block (SMB) protocol for discovery
actions.description: The actors enumerate directories and files of connected devices using Server Message Block (SMB) protocol to request services and programs from a network.

actions.name: compress collected files into RAR archives
actions.description: The actors collect relevant files into RAR archives, sometimes using a version of WinRAR brought into the victim’s environment with other malicious tooling.

actions.name: exfiltrate data to cloud storage or actor-controlled servers
actions.description: The actors exfiltrate data to web services such as cloud storage or servers not associated with their primary C2, including logging into actor-controlled cloud-based storage service accounts directly from victim networks and using PuTTY and WinSCP to exfiltrate data via FTP and other protocols.

actions.name: use tunneling tools for command and control
actions.description: The actors use tunneling tools such as 3Proxy, PLINK, and Stunnel as well as custom proxy tunneling tools to tunnel traffic over a variety of protocols from inside a network back to a C2 server, disguising malware within HTTP packets to appear as benign network traffic.

actions.name: use publicly available credential theft utilities and dual-use tools
actions.description: The actors use publicly available credential theft utilities and dual-use tools such as Mimikatz, Dumpert, and ProcDump to steal credentials.

actions.name: use customized file system enumeration tooling
actions.description: The actors used customized file system enumeration tooling written in .NET capable of receiving and executing command line arguments to enumerate directories and files and compress output files, collecting detailed information for each drive targeted on a system.

actions.name: pack late-stage tooling with VMProtect and Themida
actions.description: The actors routinely pack late-stage tooling in VMProtect and Themida to make executables difficult to discover or analyze by encrypting, encoding, or otherwise obfuscating their content.
